examples.en: My grandmother has a husky voice and a breezy way about her.
I like singers with husky voices.
My voice sounds husky, maybe from a cold.

examples.ko: 그 아저씨는 성격이 걸걸해서 누구와도 잘 지내요.
examples.en: That man has an easygoing, open personality and gets along with anyone.
The way he laughs heartily looks cool.
My throat feels husky since I got up this morning.

explain: 목소리가 굵고 약간 거칠 때 쓰는데, 아파서 갈라진 느낌뿐 아니라 시원하고 힘 있는 느낌도 있어요. 성격이 털털하고 시원시원하다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes a deep, slightly rough voice, which can sound hoarse from illness but also open and strong. It can also describe a person with an easygoing, straightforward character.

en: (traffic) control, e.g. air traffic control; also, a different word (homonym) meaning the government administrative system

examples.en: The airport control center guides the planes.
Air traffic controllers help planes land safely.
At a port, controlling ship traffic is important.
Because of bad weather, traffic control became difficult.

examples.ko: 교통 관제 시스템이 도로 상황을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: The traffic control system shows road conditions.
The plane took off following the control tower's instructions.

explain: 공항, 항구, 도로에서 움직임을 살펴보고 지시하는 일에 써요. '관제 센터', '관제탑', '관제사'처럼 합성어로 자주 나오고 혼자서는 잘 안 써요. '통제'는 막는 느낌이 있고, 관제는 안전하게 움직이도록 안내하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It refers to monitoring and directing movement at airports, ports and on roads. It mostly appears in compounds such as 관제 센터, 관제탑 and 관제사, rarely alone. 통제 often feels like restricting, while 관제 feels like guiding things to move safely.

examples.en: I go to a piano lesson studio near my house.
I sent my child to a small math tutoring place.
I heard you have to register to open a tutoring studio.
That tutoring studio has only one teacher.
When I was young, I learned calligraphy at a small lesson studio.
It's a small studio, so the class atmosphere is relaxed.

explain: 보통 '학원'보다 작은 규모로 악기, 미술, 공부 등을 가르치는 곳을 말해요. 간판에는 '교습소'라고 쓰여 있어도 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '학원'이라고 부르는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: It usually refers to a place smaller than a '학원' (academy) that teaches things like instruments, art or school subjects. Even when the sign says '교습소', many people just call it a '학원' in everyday talk.

en: communicate (by radio or signal); exchange messages

examples.en: The pilot communicates with the control tower.
The astronaut communicated with Earth every day.
I was worried because we couldn't make contact with the ship.
In the mountains, some people communicate by walkie-talkie.
After communicating with the rescue team, we learned the location.

examples.ko: 우리는 짧게 교신한 뒤에 연락이 끊겼어요.
examples.en: We were in contact briefly, and then the connection was lost.

explain: 무전기, 신호, 통신 장비로 주고받을 때 써요. 비행기, 배, 우주, 구조 상황에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서 전화나 문자로 소식을 주고받는 건 '연락하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is for exchanging messages through radios, signals, or communication equipment. It comes up often with planes, ships, space, and rescue situations. Trading news by phone or text in daily life is '연락하다'.

examples.en: At the hospital I take a number and wait in a chair.
I waited in the lobby for an hour.
Please wait over here for a moment.
There were too many people waiting, so I gave up.
I'll be waiting in the car.
Wait here, and go in when your name is called.

explain: 병원, 은행, 안내방송, 콜센터에서 자주 들어요. 친구에게는 '기다려'가 자연스러워요. '대기 번호', '대기 시간', '대기 중'처럼 붙여서도 많이 써요.
explain_en: You hear it a lot at hospitals, banks, announcements and call centers. With a friend, '기다려' is more natural. It also attaches to other words: '대기 번호' (queue number), '대기 시간' (waiting time), '대기 중' (on standby).

examples.en: The door locked with a click.
When I clicked the mouse, the screen changed.

examples.ko: 전등 스위치를 딸깍 켜자 방이 환해졌어요.
examples.en: When I flicked the light switch with a click, the room became bright.

examples.ko: 밤늦게 현관문이 딸깍 열리는 소리가 들렸어요.
examples.en: I heard the front door click open late at night.
The bag's latch made a click.
The computer keyboard makes a clicking sound.

explain: 작고 단단한 것이 걸리거나 눌릴 때 나는 소리예요. '딸각', '딸까닥'도 비슷한 소리예요. 소리가 이어지면 '딸깍딸깍'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This imitates the sound of a small hard thing latching or being pressed, like a click. '딸각' and '딸까닥' are similar sounds. When the sound repeats, say '딸깍딸깍'.

examples.en: The guard called a coworker on the walkie-talkie.
At the construction site they contact each other by walkie-talkie.
I can't hear the walkie-talkie well.
The children play with a toy walkie-talkie.
The walkie-talkie battery has run out.

examples.ko: 산에서는 휴대폰이 안 터져서 무전기를 챙겨 갔어요.
examples.en: Phones don't work in the mountains, so I took a walkie-talkie.

explain: 무전기는 휴대폰 없이 가까운 사람과 바로 말할 때 쓰는 기계예요. 말할 때 버튼을 누르는 방식이라 '무전을 치다', '교신하다'와 같이 써요. '라디오'는 듣기만 하지만 무전기는 말도 할 수 있어요.
explain_en: A 무전기 lets you talk straight to someone nearby without a phone. You press a button to speak, and it goes with '무전을 치다' and '교신하다'. A '라디오' only receives, but a 무전기 can also transmit.

examples.en: When I blew the whistle, it let out a shrill sound.
When I tapped the card, it beeped.

examples.ko: 마이크에서 삑 하는 소리가 나서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The microphone squealed and startled me.
The microwave beeps when it's done.

examples.ko: 노래 부르다가 고음에서 삑 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: My voice cracked on the high note while singing.
I heard a beep as the door locked.

explain: 호루라기나 기계에서 나는 짧고 높은 소리예요. 소리가 이어지면 '삑삑'이라고 해요. 노래할 때 음이 틀어지는 것을 '삑사리가 나다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a short, high sound from a whistle or a machine. When the sound repeats, you say '삑삑'. In singing, a cracked note is also called '삑사리가 나다'.

examples.en: A police officer helped a lost child.
I met a young police officer at the police box.

examples.ko: 아버지는 삼십 년 전에 순경으로 일을 시작하셨어요.
examples.en: My father started working as a police officer thirty years ago.
Officer, I lost my wallet.
The officer patrols the neighborhood every night.

examples.ko: 시험에 합격해서 꼭 순경이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to pass the exam and become a police officer.

explain: 경찰 계급 중 가장 낮은 편이라 길에서 만나는 경찰관이 대개 순경이에요. 평소 말할 때는 그냥 '경찰'이나 '경찰관'이라고 많이 하고, 부를 때는 '순경님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the lowest police rank, so the officers you meet on the street are often 순경. In everyday talk people usually just say 경찰 or 경찰관, and you address one as 순경님.

examples.en: The assistant director organized the shooting schedule for us.

examples.ko: 저는 영화 현장에서 조감독으로 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: I work as an assistant director on a film set.

examples.ko: 조감독은 감독을 도와 배우와 스태프를 챙겨요.
examples.en: The assistant director helps the director and looks after actors and staff.

examples.ko: 조감독에서 감독이 되려면 오랜 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to go from assistant director to director.
Assistant director, where is tomorrow's shooting location?

examples.ko: 이번 드라마의 조감독 경험이 큰 공부가 됐어요.
examples.en: Working as an assistant director on this drama taught me a lot.

explain: 영화 현장에서 쓰는 직업 이름이에요. 방송에서는 '조연출'이라고 더 자주 불러요. 높여 부를 때는 '조감독님'이라고 해요. '감독'과 달리 작품의 최종 결정은 하지 않고 현장 진행을 돕는 위치예요.
explain_en: It is a job title used on film sets. In broadcasting, '조연출' is more common. To address one politely, say '조감독님'. Unlike the '감독', this person does not make the final creative decisions and helps run the shoot.

examples.en: The two machines communicate with each other.
The spacecraft communicated with Earth.
It is a device that communicates over Wi-Fi.
You cannot communicate in the mountains.
It communicates wirelessly, so no cable is needed.
In the old days, people communicated with signal fires.

explain: 사람끼리 대화하는 '이야기하다'와 달리 기계나 기관이 정보를 주고받을 때 많이 써요. '통신사', '통신비', '통신 장애'처럼 명사 '통신'이 훨씬 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Unlike the verb for chatting, it is mostly used when machines or institutions exchange information. The noun form is much more common, as in phone carrier, phone bill and network outage.

examples.en: I called a taxi through an app.
The nurse called the patient and showed them to the exam room.
Please press the bell to call a staff member.
If it's urgent, page me at this number.

examples.ko: 번호를 호출할 때까지 자리에서 기다려 주세요.
examples.en: Please wait at your seat until your number is called.
I was surprised when the boss suddenly summoned me.

explain: 사람이나 차를 필요한 곳으로 부를 때 써요. '부르다'보다 딱딱하고, 병원 번호 부르기, 택시 앱, 직원 호출 벨처럼 시스템이 있는 곳에서 자주 나와요. 친구를 부를 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Use it for calling a person or car to where it is needed. It is stiffer than '부르다' and often appears with systems such as hospital number calls, taxi apps and staff call bells. You don't use it to call a friend.
